specification:
# WhatsApp service triage

Record each incoming WhatsApp inquiry locally with its message identifier, contact and text.

If the text contains the word URGENT, flag it for a human agent. Otherwise send a standard acknowledgement only when the contact has opted in.

If the contact has not opted in, do not send any message. Before any outgoing WhatsApp message, explicit authorization for messaging must exist.

Do not send marketing messages. A duplicate message identifier must not create a second inquiry.

Inquiries containing the word URGENT are flagged for a human agent
The otherwise branch sends a standard acknowledgement only to opted-in non-urgent contacts
No outgoing message without opt-in
Outgoing messages require explicit messaging authorization
No marketing messages

specification:
# CRM follow-up synchronization

Store each submitted follow-up request locally with its request ID and contact email, even when the CRM is unavailable.

Look up the contact in the CRM by email. Create a follow-up task in the CRM only after a matching contact has been found and the contact has consented to CRM processing.

When no matching contact exists, record the request as awaiting manual review; do not create a CRM contact.

If the CRM lookup or task creation fails, keep the local request pending and record the failure for an operator. Do not mark a request synchronized until task creation succeeds.

CRM writes require explicit authorization. Repeated submissions with the same request ID must not create another CRM task.

specification:
# Claim processing

Save each claim locally with its claim ID, customer contact and requested amount. The recorded claim is used both for eligibility review and for the customer status response.

For eligibility review, compare the requested amount with the approved policy limit. If it exceeds the limit, send the claim to a human reviewer and do not approve it automatically.

For an eligible claim, issue the customer a full refund immediately.

For an eligible claim, never issue a refund until a human reviewer approves it. These two refund instructions are both current and no precedence has been specified.

The payment provider and the permitted refund authorization are not specified. Do not execute a refund without explicit authorization. These unresolved refund decisions must block refund execution, but they must not block local claim recording or the customer status response.

Customer status responses may report that the claim is pending; they must not promise that a refund has been issued.
